---
title: "One Selected Network, Direct and HB Realizations"
---

::: {.callout-warning}
## Accepted backends; CONVERGING parameter spaces

The Direct and harmonic-balance meanings on this page remain accepted. This
page explains their relationship. Per-point Parameter System binding is a
separate `CONVERGING` target. Backend rows, equations, capabilities, and
failures belong to the linked contracts.
:::

## The analysis question comes before the backend

Once a complete Plan and the required `NetworkViewRef` exist, a reader may
ask for a small-signal Direct response, a pump-off HB response, or a supported
driven HB case. Direct and HB are two realizations of that selected network.
Neither backend owns the public circuit topology.

Both paths must bind the same expanded Plan, component identities, logical Port
attachments, and selected View. A backend either realizes that input faithfully
within its declared capability or fails closed.

When a request supplies a `ParameterSet` or `ParameterSpace`, each point first
binds a complete effective value set to the same Plan and then realizes the
selected View. Direct and HB may reuse compatible preparation inside one Julia
process, but neither may reuse a nominal parameter-dependent matrix or treat a
previous point as the circuit authority.

## What stays common {#direct-and-hb-selected-network}

The public S/Y/Z surface uses the selected View's ordered Port and coordinate
meaning. One logical Port remains one authored boundary even though Direct and
HB lower it through different internal matrices. A reader does not author a
second HB-specific circuit or rename the Port for the solver.

The Result from each request preserves:

- the Plan and selected-View lineage;
- Port order, direction, reference impedance, and frequency convention;
- the backend and exact grid used; and
- its own receipt and numerical evidence.

## What remains different

Direct compiles the selected network to its C/K/G and wave-boundary
realization. HB keeps the declared nonlinear realization and case/truncation
meaning. Pump-off HB can therefore provide a comparable linear response when
the topology and observable match, but it is still independent evidence rather
than a second implementation of the Direct Result.

Capabilities may differ. A component or selected View that Direct supports is
not automatically HB-capable, and SCNSim does not weaken the Plan silently to
make both run.

Direct and HB also keep independent frequency grids. Presentation may show
their curves together, but it performs no interpolation and does not imply
pointwise numerical comparison where frequency points differ. Magnitude-only
similarity is not full complex-network agreement.

Engineer [Chapter 4](../../examples/engineer/chapter-04/06-optional-hb.qmd)
applies this distinction to one transformed View: its named Direct Result uses
the declared 5.5/6.0/6.5 GHz grid, while pump-off HB uses the separate
5.4/5.9/6.4 GHz grid. The page presents both Results independently and makes
no overlay, interpolation, or new agreement claim.

## A diagram does not choose either realization

The Automatic Semantic Circuit Diagram Layout System (ASCDLS) projects the
original authored Plan or its compiler expansion. It is not aware of the
selected analysis View and cannot choose Direct, HB, a pump case, or a Result.
A compiled diagram can explain lowering evidence, but it remains a Plan
projection rather than the circuit evaluated after PTC, transforms, or
retention.

## What this concept deliberately excludes

This page does not make JosephsonCircuits the topology authority, invent a fake
Direct backend marker, imply arbitrary bias-point linearization, merge native
frequency grids, or claim that comparable plots validate a physical model. It
also does not redefine the signed-frequency, state, case, or failure contracts.
Complete RLGC values remain supported only where the declared backend and
operation support them; this candidate does not perform baseline-root
continuation across changing RLGC matrices or imply that such continuation is
mathematically impossible.
